Right: the joined tree, with the new root 1 in the accent color and edges in the accent color to the old roots, now 3 and 5. The path keeps its shape as 2, 3, 4, and badges give each node's old label: a, b, c and x." width="100%"} Given trees with a chosen root each, this builds the tree that has a fresh root node with an edge to every one of those roots: the trees become the subtrees of the new root. It is the basic way to grow rooted trees from smaller ones, so for example two complete binary trees of height `h` joined this way give one of height `h + 1`, and it is how `from_nested_tuple()` builds a tree from its code. The nodes are renumbered, since labels from different trees may clash: the new root is node `1`, labeled `str(first_label)`, and then come the nodes of each tree in turn, in ascending ID order, with IDs `2`, `3`, ... and labels counting up from `first_label + 1`. With `label_attribute=`, each copied node remembers its old label (or its ID, if it had no label) under that attribute. Node and edge attributes and edge weights are copied. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [rooted_trees]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of `(tree, root)` pairs: a `Graph` and the node (ID or label) of it that becomes a child of the new root. The trees must be all undirected or all directed; they are not checked for being trees. [label_attribute]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of a node attribute in which to store the old label of every copied node. If `None` (the default), the old labels are dropped. [first_label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The number in the root's label; the other labels count up from it. Defaults to `1`, so labels match the node IDs (NetworkX's default is `0`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new tree with directedness and weighting of the first tree (undirected and unweighted for an empty list, which gives a single node). On directed trees the new edges point from the new root to the old roots, and on weighted trees they weigh `1.0`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a root is not in its tree, or the trees mix directed and undirected graphs. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The join copies every node and edge once, so it runs in $O(V + E)$ time for the total size of the trees. NetworkX numbers the nodes the same way, tree by tree in node order, but adds the root last; here the root comes first (ID `1`), which keeps the root easy to find. With `first_label=0`, the labels are NetworkX's. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Joining a path and a single node under a new root: ::: {#8e283cc0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["a", "b", "c"]).add_edges([("a", "b"), ("b", "c")]) leaf = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["x"]) joined = ec.Graph.join_trees([(path, "b"), (leaf, "x")], label_attribute="old") joined.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['2--3', '3--4', '1--3', '1--5'] ``` ::: ::: The new root is `"1"`, joined to the old roots `b` (now `"3"`) and `x` (now `"5"`). The old labels are kept in the `old` attribute: ::: {#d8eee5bb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} { joined.get_label_from_id(n): joined.get_node(n).attributes["old"] for n in sorted(joined.get_node_ids(limit=None))[1:] } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'2': 'a', '3': 'b', '4': 'c', '5': 'x'} ``` ::: ::: Two complete binary trees of height 2, joined at their roots, form one of height 3: ::: {#51cd84fe .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} half = ec.Graph.from_nested_tuple((((), ()), ((), ()))) whole = ec.Graph.join_trees([(half, "1"), (half, "1")]) whole.to_nested_tuple("1") == ((((), ()), ((), ())), (((), ()), ((), ()))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
